modes.label: General-purpose CPU VM (c1a/c2a), on-demand
modes.note: $0.04/vCPU-hr incl. 4 GiB RAM/vCPU (c1a.2x 2 vCPU/8 GB ... c1a.176x 176/704 GB; c2a in eu-norway1-a, c2a.172x max). No local disk: mandatory 128 GiB OS persistent disk $0.08/GiB-month extra ($10.24/VM-month, billed even when stopped). Per-second billing while Running; Creating state (up to 1 min) not billed. Some types/regions 'restricted', contact sales.

modes.label: Storage-optimized CPU VM (s1a/s2a), on-demand
modes.note: $0.09/vCPU-hr; s1a.20x 20 vCPU/176 GB/1x12.8 TB NVMe ... s1a.160x. Local NVMe is ephemeral (erased on stop/start). s2a (eu-norway1-a) starts at s2a.10x 10 vCPU/86 GB/15.36 TB -> $0.90/h.

caveats: GPU VM bundle includes matching CPU/RAM; billing per second in running state including lifecycle scripts. Stopped VM compute free, retained 128GiB OS disk $0.08/GiB-month until deletion. Reserved commitment bills in every state. Spot quote via sales. No network transfer charges currently.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

2026-09-28: H100/H200/A100 SXM VMs exist only as 8x types (docs.crusoecloud.com: h100-80gb-sxm-ib.8x 176 vCPU / 960 GB); priced per GPU with gpu_min_count 8. Multi-GPU PCIe A100/L40S VMs priced with gpu_min_count = GPUs per VM. alt removed from all GPU VMs.

Every VM has a fixed 128 GiB OS persistent disk ($0.08/GiB-month = $10.24/VM-month) billed while the VM exists, running or stopped; OS disks cannot be resized. Custom images billed at $0.08/GiB-month of used data. Shared disks $0.07/GiB-month (min 1 TiB). Object storage $0.06/GiB-month. Container registry $0.10/GiB-month. Managed Kubernetes $0.10/cluster-hour.
GPU and s1a/s2a local NVMe (ephemeral) disks are erased when the VM is stopped and restarted; only the OS disk and persistent/shared disks survive a stop.
Introductory $5 free credit applies only to Managed AI (Serverless Inference / Fine-Tuning), not to VMs. Enabling billing for VMs requires a valid non-prepaid credit card.

Reservations (sales) bill for the whole term in every state; usage above the reserved GPU count at any instant bills on-demand; unused capacity does not roll over. Enterprise support tier is free only with qualifying annual commit/reservation.

fleet.notes: Project-specific CPU/GPU instance quotas and organization project/user quotas are visible in Console Admin > Usage > Quotas. Contact support for increases. Stopped instances do not consume instance quota. New-account defaults and review timing unpublished; example 4-H100 quotas are illustrative, not defaults.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: The disks are erased when the physical server reboots, or the VM is stopped and restarted, or if there are any other hardware or software failures.
snapshot_auto.note: Plain VMs: stop keeps only the OS disk and attached persistent/shared disks (that is persistent_disk); local NVMe on GPU/s1a VMs is erased; no memory/state capture. No snapshot or backup feature appears anywhere in the docs sitemap.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Once customers have created a virtual machine (VM) from a base image and customized it with preferred configurations and software, they can stop the VM and create a custom image from its boot disk.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Only form is a custom image of the OS/boot disk (crusoe compute images create --vm-name); VM must be SHUTOFF ('Create a custom image from a VM while it is not SHUTOFF' is not allowed); disk only, no memory; new VMs can boot from it (template-like), region/project scoped. No snapshots of persistent data disks or running VMs documented.

harness_api.quote: Crusoe provides flexible options for running AI workloads. You can train, deploy, and run inference workloads using Crusoe's managed infrastructure or your own infrastructure.
harness_api.note: Crusoe is a GPU IaaS cloud (VMs, Kubernetes/Slurm clusters, Managed AI serverless inference/fine-tuning). The full docs sitemap has no product for driving a coding agent harness (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) inside a sandbox - only a management MCP server (query/inspect infra) and CLI/Terraform for VM lifecycle. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_allowlist.quote: `ingress` is "outside world to the VM" and `egress` is "VM to the outside world"
egress_allowlist.note: VPC firewall rules: allow-only, implicit deny, five-tuple (IP/CIDR + ports, tcp/udp/icmp). Default VPC ships default-allow-tcp-udp-egress / default-allow-icmp-egress which you can delete for default-deny; custom VPCs start with everything denied. CLI: '--direction ... Allowed directions: `INGRESS`, `EGRESS`' (the Terraform section of the managing page still says ingress is the only direction; stale). No domain rules. Outbound SMTP 25/465/2525 blocked by default.

egress_http_rules.quote: VPC Firewall Rules rely on a five-tuple to filter L3 traffic and determine if it is allowed to pass
egress_http_rules.note: L3/L4 only; no HTTP-level egress rules.

ingress_rules.quote: VPC Firewall Rules allow developers to granularly control access to VPC networks, subnets, and individual VMs.
ingress_rules.note: Ingress rules by source IP/CIDR and port; default VPC allows SSH from the internet (deletable); ingress destination must be the VM's private IP. Load balancers also available.

guest_firewall.note: Full VMs (not containers) with Ubuntu images and sudo user 'ubuntu' (root login deprecated); customers can even change kernels on custom images.

secret_proxy.quote: Control who can access your organization and how—manage users, enforce SSO and MFA, review audit logs, and secure your data with API keys and customer-managed encryption keys.
secret_proxy.note: Crusoe's security/identity docs cover org auth (SSO/MFA), API keys for calling Crusoe's own API, and customer-managed keys for data-at-rest encryption - no credential-injecting HTTP proxy that keeps third-party secrets out of the VM. Full docs sitemap has no secrets-manager/proxy page; on Crusoe VMs, secrets are only env vars/mounted files as already recorded.

volume_attach.quote: Persistent Disks are remote block storage volumes that are attached to a virtual machine.
volume_attach.note: 1 GiB-10 TiB, up to 16 disks per VM incl. OS disk, attach/detach while running or stopped, $0.08/GiB-month. Shared Disks 1-1000 TiB, up to 8 per VM, $0.07/GiB-month.

volume_shared.quote: Shared Disks are shared network filesystems, designed to be accessed from many virtual machines concurrently.
volume_shared.note: Shared Disks: read-write NFS (VAST), min 1 TiB, not encrypted in transit. Persistent block disks can also multi-attach but only read-only: 'can be attached to multiple VMs in `read-only` mode' (CLI/Terraform only).

isolation.note: Crusoe Cloud Security Advisories on the Trust Center name cloud-hypervisor as the hypervisor component patched/validated; VMs are full-VM instances (root, custom kernel-capable), consistent with cloud-hypervisor-based isolation.

image_oci.quote: Custom images are customer-managed, modified versions of curated images... Custom images can only be created from the boot disks of a VM.
image_oci.note: VMs boot from Crusoe VM disk images (curated/custom, boot-disk based), not from Docker/OCI container images.

egress_ip_type.quote: --public-ip-type string     Public IP type. Allowed values: `static`, `dynamic`
egress_ip_type.note: Public IPv4 addresses are standard datacenter IPs assignable as static or dynamic; no residential/mobile IP offering.

fork.quote: Once customers have created a virtual machine (VM) from a base image and customized it with preferred configurations and software, they can stop the VM and create a custom image from its boot disk... customers can select their newly created custom image as the base image [for subsequent VMs]
fork.note: Cloning is via custom image of a stopped VM's boot disk, then launching new VMs from it (template-style fork), not a live 1-click machine clone API.

fork_running.quote: Customers cannot do the following: 1. Create a custom image from a VM while it is not SHUTOFF.
fork_running.note: The source VM must be stopped (SHUTOFF) before a custom image (used to spawn new VMs) can be created.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: they can stop the VM and create a custom image from its boot disk
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Custom images capture only the boot disk contents; no memory/process state is captured or restored.

pause_resume.quote: A stopped VM retains all data stored on that VM. An on-demand stopped VM is not billed
pause_resume.note: Start/stop lifecycle: stopping a VM halts compute billing (only the 128GB OS disk keeps billing) while retaining data; starting resumes it.

wake_on_request.quote: Use the `compute vms <stop|start|reset>` command to change the state of an already existing VM.
wake_on_request.note: State changes (start/stop) are explicit API/CLI/console actions; no documented automatic wake-on-incoming-request mechanism.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Use the `compute vms <stop|start|reset>` command to change the state of an already existing VM.
auto_stop_idle.note: Only manual/explicit stop is documented; no automatic idle-timeout stop feature found.

live_resize.quote: Currently, only the "network_interfaces" and "disks" of the instance can be changed. Changes to other fields of the instance will force a re-creation of the instance (deletion and then creation of a new instance).
live_resize.note: VM type (CPU/RAM/GPU) is not documented as changeable on a live running VM without recreation.

agent_harnesses.quote: Curated images are images provided by Crusoe Cloud... These images contain a base operating system, e.g. Ubuntu, and additional software where specified
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: curated images ship OS/GPU-driver/docker/slurm stacks; no coding-agent (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) templates documented.

own_agent_api.quote: Crusoe Cloud provides a high-performance, sustainable cloud platform with the latest hardware.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (GPU/CPU IaaS; no first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent)

inbound_https.quote: Crusoe Cloud currently offers L4 passthrough load balancers... allowing you to distribute TCP or UDP traffic across one or more backends.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope for managed HTTPS URLs; only raw public IPv4/TCP/UDP (VM public IP or L4 load balancer) is provided, no managed HTTPS termination/URL.

windows.quote: Curated images are images provided by Crusoe Cloud... These images contain a base operating system, e.g. Ubuntu
windows.note: Only Ubuntu/Linux curated images are documented; no Windows VM image or type exists.

macos.quote: Curated images are images provided by Crusoe Cloud... These images contain a base operating system, e.g. Ubuntu
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Crusoe is an x86/ARM Linux GPU cloud, no macOS instances documented.

self_host.quote: Crusoe Cloud provides a high-performance, sustainable cloud platform with the latest hardware.
self_host.note: Crusoe Cloud is a managed multi-tenant cloud service on Crusoe's own datacenters; no self-hosted/on-prem software distribution is documented.

byoc.quote: Crusoe Cloud provides a high-performance, sustainable cloud platform with the latest hardware.
byoc.note: No bring-your-own-cloud/account deployment model is documented; Crusoe runs its own datacenters/hardware.

open_source.quote: Crusoe Cloud provides a high-performance, sustainable cloud platform with the latest hardware.
open_source.note: Crusoe Cloud is a proprietary managed cloud platform; no OSI-licensed core product is documented.

hipaa.note: Trust Center lists a HIPAA Implementation Guide (behind 'Request access') under Implementation Guides, indicating HIPAA-eligible workloads/BAA support; document contents not independently viewable.

eu_data_residency.note: Crusoe operates EU regions (eu-iceland1-a, eu-norway1-a) where VMs/data can be kept.

max_session_h.quote: VMs are charged based on the time the machine is in the `running` state (per second).
max_session_h.note: On-demand VMs run until explicitly stopped/deleted by the customer; no maximum session duration is documented (reservation term limits are a separate commercial constraint).

nested_virt.quote: Crusoe manages: Physical hardware (GPUs, CPUs), data centers, power, cooling, hypervisor / bare-metal provisioning, and InfiniBand RDMA networking fabric.
nested_virt.note: Crusoe VMs are guests on Crusoe's own cloud-hypervisor/KVM stack (guest kernel package literally named `*-kvm`, e.g. `5.4.0-1061-kvm`). Nothing in the full docs sitemap (images, VM overview, security/identity, networking) mentions exposing /dev/kvm or enabling nested virtualization inside a guest VM; not documented as available.

lang_python.note: Crusoe's own operational docs run `python3 <script>` directly on a freshly-created VM with no prior 'apt install python3' step, confirming Python 3 ships on the curated Ubuntu 22.04/20.04 base images used by all Crusoe VMs.

lang_node.quote: Curated images are images provided by Crusoe Cloud and made available to all developers on the platform. These images contain a base operating system, e.g. Ubuntu, and additional software where specified... `ubuntu22.04` Ubuntu 22.04 base image.
lang_node.note: The full curated-image list (ubuntu22.04, ubuntu22.04-nvidia-sxm-docker, ubuntu22.04-nvidia-pcie-docker, ubuntu22.04-nvidia-slurm, ubuntu-rocm) only calls out NVIDIA/ROCm drivers, InfiniBand support, and a Docker runtime as included extras; no image or doc mentions a preinstalled Node.js runtime. Crusoe is an IaaS VM provider (root access, custom images) so Node.js can be installed by the user, but it is not shipped out of the box.

usage_api.quote: GET /organizations/{organization_id}/billing/costs returns daily spend for a specified organization by project; GET /organizations/{organization_id}/billing/export-productline returns a CSV containing costs for resources in a given period, with optional filtering by projects, product_lines, regions,
usage_api.note: granularity: per-project; cost: yes; Crusoe's REST API provides multiple endpoints for usage/cost retrieval: billing/costs returns real-time daily spend by project; billing/export-productline exports CSV by product line, project, region; usage endpoints support project-level and resource-level filtering, enabling per-sandbox billing (each VM/resource can be tagged/identified by project_id and resource_type for cost attribution)
